articles.title: People Are Acting Weird As Hell During Fortnite’s Treasure Hunt
articles.dek: The search for the Pirate Shop token has dramatically changed the flow of a Fortnite match.
articles.excerpt: Fortnite's new Treasure Hunters season is such a massive success that the battle royale's player counts are five times higher than last week, because everybody and their mothers want in on the search for Tim Sweeney's golden ticket. It grants everything in the item shop for free, both for two weeks this year and two more weeks in 2027. That means two things: Most of the people playing Fortnite right now haven't been playing recently, and folks aren't necessarily playing to win. The way the hunt works is that every time you or one of your teammates opens a treasure chest, there's a chance that a rare prize will be granted to the whole party. It could be a golden A$AP Rocky skin, a Mercedes G-Wagon skin, or the extremely elusive Pirate Shop Access token, which makes virtually the whole shop free. The hunt for that Pirate Shop token in particular has changed the way people play BR. The primary goal for many players is now not to win, but to open as many chests as possible in pursuit of the token. Since your whole squad gets any of these treasures regardless of who found them, four-player Squad fills have been the place to go for the hunt--understandably, most of us don't have enough friends who want to play Fortnite 12 hours a day to keep the squad filled on our own. Playing Squad fills has always been a bit of crapshoot in terms of the quality of your teammates, but the new treasure hunt has folks acting a lot more erratic than usual. While playing entirely too much Fortnite this week, I've identified a few player profiles--let's call them recurring characters--that I've been encountering over and over again. articles.title: The Best Warzone Perks May Surprise You After The MW4 Overhaul
articles.dek: Warzone perks are changing with Modern Warfare 4's integration.
articles.excerpt: Modern Warfare 4 integrates with Warzone for Season 1, adding MW4's full weapon pool, attachments, and other new gear into battle royale. The big update also overhauls Warzone's perk system, including the introduction of the powerful new "Elite" perks. In this guide, we'll explain how perks work for this new year of Warzone and include some recommended picks for your next match. How perks work in Warzone for MW4 For Modern Warfare 4, there are a total of 18 perks available for Warzone. The first 15 are options you can choose for your custom loadouts, fitting into one of three different perk slots. The remaining three are new Elite perks, and you can acquire one during a match as an additional fourth perk. Elite perks are a special perk type that are only discoverable within a match. These can be gained through various means, including Buy Station purchases or as rewards for completing Supply Run contracts. Only one Elite Perk can be equipped at a time. Additionally, Tactical Sprint is no longer a perk this year and everyone will have this movement be default. Warzone's new create-a-class menu All perk 1 options Field Medic This perk allows you to quickly revive allies to full health, and you gain the same benefits. You also receive increased health while downed. Hunter Hunter lets you track enemy footprints, sense nearby enemies, and become alert when aimed at. It also outlines enemies you shoot for a duration. Stocked This perk lets you carry an additional lethal and tactical equipment item and see a visible trajectory when you throw it. It deals increased explosive damage from equipment and launchers. articles.title: GTA 6 Is Going All Out On Details You Might Never Even Notice
articles.dek: The more you look at GTA 6, the more impressive it looks.
articles.excerpt: It's the smallest details that stand out most in Grand Theft Auto 6, and thanks to all the screenshots that developer Rockstar Games has posted since the game was officially announced, there's been no shortage of stuff to analyze. Last week, senior video producer Jake Dekker grabbed all 99 of those official screenshots--with the number of images increasing this week thanks to a new screenshot dump--and started going through each and every single one of them. He found plenty of cool little secrets hidden in each image, from legal tender celebrating paranoia to surprisingly realistic flesh, and this week, he's back with another look at GTA 6's impressive attention to detail. Some of these include colorful iguana lizards dotted around Vice City, references to real-life abandoned bridge projects, and local hangouts where you can catch some downtime between heists. Check it for yourself in the video below: https://youtu.be/oxqys4Nm4Cs Some of the other cool secrets hidden inside of these screenshots include vibrant underwater environments with scuba gear that looks very authentic, and co-protagonist Lucia's high-thread-count gym gear--maybe Jason could learn a thing or two from her about proper gym etiquette. The screenshots also show off Rockstar's technical skills for camera angles, lighting effects, and reflections, making each scene pop when you start to examine them closely. If these screenshots are a solid indicator of what to expect, it looks like GTA 6 could be one of the best-looking games of the year, which is no small feat considering that games like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Resident Evil Requiem, and 007 First Light have pushed the line for realistic video game graphics in 2026.
